chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn Ma'sum) from Fadala from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskhan from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Indeed, when you call the Adhan and establish the Iqamah, two rows of angels pray behind you. And if you establish the Iqamah without an Adhan, one row of angels prays behind you.'

key_terms.أَذَّنْتَ: You call the Adhan (call to prayer)
key_terms.أَقَمْتَ: You establish the Iqamah (second call to prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of angels for performing the Adhan and Iqamah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the metaphysical dimension of the Adhan, where the physical act of calling prayer invites a visible or spiritual presence of angels who join the congregation. The distinction between performing both Adhan and Iqamah versus only Iqamah underscores the superior merit of the complete ritual sequence, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the detailed observance of prophetic traditions. It serves as a reminder that the Mu'adhin not only calls humans to prayer but also orchestrates a celestial assembly, enhancing the spiritual atmosphere of the mosque.
